newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi to launch digital video camera for PC use.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi to launch digital video camera for PC use.

text.p: Japan's Hitachi Ltd said on Monday it will launch a digital video camera next month that will be able to produce high-quality footage for editing and viewing on personal computers.

Hitachi said its new digital video camera system, to be released on February 22 in Japan, would be the first product of its kind to be able to offer such video manipulation by PC without the need for expensive additional equipment.
The new camera will allow computer users to produce video material for displaying on the Internet, it said.

The camera, designed on the Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG) format, enables users to transfer recorded video to a personal computer and use the computer to produce, edit and view full-motion video, Hitachi said in a statement.

The new product can compress recorded video data to one-hundredth of the original, compared with conventional digital video cameras, which compresses data to one-fifth. This high compression ratio allows full-motion video recorded by the camera to be manipulated on an average PC, Hitachi said.

With the new camera, "the average PC user will be able to produce video on a PC and add it to a Web site homepage, for example, or send it attached to e-mail", senior executive managing director Etsuhiko Shoyama said in the statement.
The camera will be priced at 132,000 yen ($1,109), while the accessory kit and data storage card for recording video will be priced at 16,000 yen ($134) and 75,000 yen ($630).

Initial production is expected to be 10,000 units per month, the statement said. A digital colour printer will also be released on February 22, the company said. Hitachi said it aimed to start marketing the camera in the United States in March and in Europe in June. ($1=119 yen)
